pr.title: Plan arming and the live voice path, and let field keys play tracks in unison (arming.md chunk 1)
pr.head: e22af1ee0bdad98ecc349afc794556b19392e6b8

summary: field keys turns the computer keyboard into a MIDI source named Field Keys. Given an instrument, a SuperCollider program on the project's shared/instruments/ shelf, it also starts a voice host: an sclang process that boots its own scsynth on the output device and plays the program's voice from every MIDI source. Until this change it took exactly one program, so to hear the part a track plays you had to know which program the track's record entry names, and you could not name the track at all.

This pull request does two things. It writes the plan for arming, which lets you choose the tracks to play or record together, and it rewrites the stub plan for the live voice path, which would let a track's effects process what you play. Then it builds arming's first chunk: field keys takes any number of targets, resolves a track to the instrument its record entry names, and plays every resolved instrument at once from one voice host.

1. You name targets. field keys creek/track:keys creek/track:bass. A target with track: in it is a track; anything else is an instrument, resolved as before.
  2. Each track resolves to one MIDI track. A MIDI track is a track whose record: entry names an instrument, takes or not. A bus resolves to the one MIDI track under it; a bus with several refuses and lists them, so you name the ones you mean.
  3. One voice host plays them in unison. It loads every program, renames each SynthDef for its place in the list so two programs that name their voices alike both play, and starts one voice per program on every key.
  4. The line says what is not heard. The voice still plays straight to the device, so a bus's inserts are skipped, and the instrument's line ends · dry: the effects on keys-bus are not heard yet.

The review of this head opened two findings, shown as flags below: a bus that places its one MIDI track twice is refused as if it held two, and the plan's §2.1 describes an instrument line and a reload the code does not have.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• MIDI track: a track whose record: entry has instrument:. It plays that instrument from its MIDI takes, and it is a MIDI track before it has any.
  • Bus: a track whose inputs include other tracks, as - track: keys.
  • Insert: an effect on a track, such as an EQ, which runs inside the daemon field-audiod.
  • Voice host: sc/voice-host.scd running in sclang, with its own scsynth on the output device.
  • Armed: chosen to play or record. In this chunk you arm by naming targets on the command line.
  • Dry: heard without the inserts on the tracks you named, because the voice skips the daemon.

cards.title: What this leaves for later
cards.html:
• Recording several tracks in one pass is arming chunk 2: an arm set in the daemon, one latch, one take per track.
  • A lasting arm through field arm and the UI is chunk 3, after Justin decides where it lives.
  • Hearing the effects waits on the live-supercollider plan, still a draft with the transport undecided.
  • Criterion 4 by ear: two instruments sounding one key is still owed; nobody has listened yet.

groups.title: The arming plan
groups.kicker: What it means to arm tracks, and the three chunks that build it
intro: Arming is a set of tracks you choose to play or record. The plan has you arm tracks by naming them, because field keys and field record already take targets, and it puts a lasting arm, set with field arm or the UI, last, once Justin decides where it lives.

Read §2.1 for what this pull request builds, §3 for the decisions with the alternatives they beat, and §9 for what chunk 1 settled. The plan is in-progress, which claims the work is ready to build, so every open question has to be answered or deferred. All three in §7 are deferred explicitly, with who decides and when.

checks.text: Two calls are Justin's: you choose what is armed, and armed tracks play in unison. The rest of §3 is decided in the plan "for Justin's review", so any of it can be overturned in review: refusing a bus over several MIDI tracks rather than arming all of them, one voice host rather than one per instrument, and audio inputs in the order you name the tracks.

files.note: The new plan. §2.1 is chunk 1, built here; §2.2 and the daemon rows of §2.3 are chunk 2; §9 records what chunk 1 settled and what is still owed.

checks.text: Review finding (open): this step says the line reads keys: juno · bass: bass live at … and names the bus creek/track:keys-bus. The code prints keys (juno) + bass (bass) live at … and · dry: the effects on keys-bus are not heard yet, as docs/keys.md shows. Step 3 also says a save reloads "it", where the host reloads every program.
Readiness: each of the three questions is deferred explicitly, to Justin before chunk 3, or until someone needs loop takes on two parts or a split-zone controller. None blocks chunk 1 or 2.
This background describes the code before the change: resolveInstrument now lives in src/keys/targets.ts, and the voice host holds voiceDefs. §9 says so.

groups.title: Resolving targets to instruments
groups.kicker: How a track target becomes the program the voice host plays
intro: resolveKeysTargets turns the command line into a list of armed instruments: a program's absolute path, the track it plays for when it came from a track, and the tracks between the one you named and the MIDI track whose inserts you will not hear. An instrument target goes through resolveInstrument, the same rule as before, which moved here from src/commands/keys.ts unchanged.

A track target goes through resolveRecordTarget, the label parser field record uses, which loads and validates the whole project. Then midiTracksUnder walks down the track's track: inputs to the tracks whose record entries name an instrument. One found track is armed; none or several is an error.

checks.text: A track's instrument resolves the way the build resolves a record entry's instrument: for rendering a MIDI take, so field keys plays the same program the take renders through.

files.note: New. Holds the instrument rule and shelf listing moved from the command, and the track rule this chunk adds.

checks.text: Review finding (open): midiTracksUnder pushes a MIDI track once per track: input that reaches it, so a bus that places keys at [1] and again at [5], the way bed.yaml places phrase three times, exits with 2 MIDI tracks are under keys-loop … creek/track:keys, creek/track:keys. A bus over both keys-bus and the keys under it fails the same way. The fix is to key the found tracks by name and merge the effects of every path.

Review finding (open), second site: add keeps the first entry for a track and drops a later target's unheardEffects, so field keys creek/track:keys creek/track:keys-bus shows no dry note while the reverse order names keys-bus.

This branch does not run: resolveRecordTarget calls loadValid, which already refuses a record entry whose instrument file is missing. Checked with instrument: nope, which fails with instrument file not found: shared/instruments/nope.scd.

The dry list holds only the tracks from the one you named down to the MIDI track. Naming keys directly under an EQ'd keys-bus shows no dry note, which matches the plan's "when a target was a bus with effects".

groups.title: Unison in one voice host
groups.kicker: The host takes a list of programs and starts a voice from each on every key
intro: The voice host is a SuperCollider script that field keys runs in sclang. It boots its own scsynth, loads a program's voice, a SynthDef with freq, amp, gate, and out controls, and hands MIDI to sc/voicer.scd, which decides when voices start and stop.

The host now reads FIELD_INSTRUMENTS, a JSON list of program paths, instead of one path. It renames each SynthDef to field<index>_<name>, so two programs that both call their voice \bassKey do not replace each other, and its start callback returns a list of synths, one per program. The voicer needs no change, because it stores whatever start returns and passes it back to set and release.

checks.text: One host serves every armed instrument, so there is one scsynth to boot, restart, and quit. A rate restart adds every renamed SynthDef again through addAll; a reload loads every program and keeps all the old voices if any fails.

files.note: The list of programs, the renaming in loadAll, a voice that is a list of synths, and a reload of every program.

checks.text: Checked in sclang with no server: juno.scd and bass.scd loaded through voice-load.scd as field0_junoKey and field1_bassKey, three programs that share bassKey got three distinct names, and paths with a space, a double quote, and non-ASCII letters survived the JSON list.
One broken program holds back every reload: a fix saved to another program does not load until the broken one does. §9 records this as intended.
The header, at lines 13 and 14, still says /field/reload loads "the program" again; it loads every program.

files.note: instruments replaces instrument in the options, and goes to the host as JSON.
The stub host records FIELD_INSTRUMENTS, and the resolveInstrument tests import it from its new home.

groups.title: The command and its line
groups.kicker: field keys takes targets, and its instrument line names each armed track
intro: field keys shows an instrument line above its status line, saying whether the voice is starting, live, or restarting. With several targets, the line joins one name per armed instrument with +: a track shows as keys (juno), an instrument given by program as juno. When a track you named has inserts the voice skips, the line ends with the dry note.
The command dedupes programs before it starts the host, so naming juno and a track that plays juno starts one juno voice per key, and it watches each program so a save reloads the host.

files.note: Takes targets, starts one host with the deduped programs, watches each program, and builds the line from armedName and the dry list.

checks.text: No test covers armedName or the dry note, though docs/keys.md documents the exact line.

files.note: keys [targets...] is variadic and optional, so field keys with nothing still runs as a MIDI source only.
A new "Play a track" section: naming tracks, mixing them with instruments, the bus rule, and the dry note.

groups.title: The live voice path, planned
groups.kicker: A draft plan for hearing a track's effects on what you play
intro: A track's inserts run inside the daemon field-audiod, and the voice plays in its own scsynth, so nothing you play passes through them. The plan names two obstacles: nothing carries audio between Field's processes, and a live session renders every track except the output track in full when it loads, which a voice played by hand cannot be.

It proposes an input window kind, live tracks that mix and run their chains in the audio callback, and a shared-memory ring that a small scsynth plugin, FieldOut, writes and the daemon reads. It weighs that against embedding libscsynth in the daemon and against a loopback device.

checks.text: The plan is a draft, so it claims no readiness, and its three questions, the transport, live tracks with the transport stopped, and several armed tracks under one bus, do not gate this change. It does not reverse keyboard-instrument.md §3 "Straight to the device", which handed this work to live-supercollider and kept the voice host's interface, as this plan does.
